boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Iowa State spaces for quiet study, group work, media production, community gatherings, hands-on projects, and restorative breaks.

cards.title: Book a Quiet Booth at Central Parks
cards.subtitle: Reservable focus pods inside Parks Library’s Learning Connections Center
cards.notes: Reserve a pod for focused work, an interview, or a video call; bring your device and use the adjustable desk, outlets, and campus Wi-Fi.
cards.short_summary: Sound-dampening library pods offer students a more private setting for concentration and digital meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State’s library says Central Parks has sound-dampening study pods with adjustable desks, power, Wi-Fi, and reservations of up to three hours for ISU NetID holders.
cards.source_title: Central Parks offers booth-style study spaces including ADA-compliant option
cards.access_notes: Located in the first-floor Learning Connections Center at Parks Library; an ISU NetID is required to reserve a pod for up to three hours.

cards.title: Spread Out in the Learning Connections Center
cards.subtitle: Computer workstations and reservable collaboration rooms on Parks Library’s first floor
cards.notes: Use the wired tables for a group project, reserve a whiteboard room, or move to a computer workstation when a laptop screen is not enough.
cards.short_summary: The LCC combines group tables, computers, scanners, varied seating, and reservable rooms in one flexible work area.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library identifies the Learning Connections Center as a first-floor collaborative space with 24 PCs, 12 Macs, scanners, wired tables, and three reservable group rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of Parks Library, north of the lobby beyond the glass wall; collaboration rooms require reservations.

cards.title: Record a Presentation in Studio 2B
cards.subtitle: A bookable One Button Studio and Lightboard in Parks Library
cards.notes: Book a station before filming a class presentation or interview, bring a USB drive for file transfer, and avoid green clothing at the One Button Studio.
cards.short_summary: Students can produce polished videos or livestreams with built-in cameras, monitors, lighting, and presentation tools.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library says Studio 2B is available to students, faculty, and staff and contains a One Button Studio and Lightboard for recording or livestreaming video.
cards.access_notes: Located on Parks Library’s lower level inside Maps, Media, and Microforms; users should book a time before arriving.

cards.title: Switch to Complete Quiet in the Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Parks Library’s designated silent-study room
cards.notes: Take individual reading or writing to Room 298 when conversation is distracting, and keep the room’s complete-quiet expectation for everyone.
cards.short_summary: High ceilings, natural light, and ample tables define the library’s only designated quiet study room.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library identifies the second-floor Reading Room, Room 298, as Parks Library’s only designated quiet study space and asks users to refrain completely from conversation.
cards.access_notes: Room 298 on the second floor of Parks Library; complete quiet is expected, so conversations should happen elsewhere.

cards.title: Find Several Ways to Work at the Multicultural Center
cards.subtitle: Study nooks, meeting space, computers, and reflection rooms in the Memorial Union
cards.notes: Choose a study nook for solo work, meet in the library area, or reserve a reflection room when a small group needs a quieter setting.
cards.short_summary: This community space supports studying, informal meetings, relaxation, and private reflection within the Memorial Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State Multicultural Student Affairs says the center is available to the university community and provides eight study nooks, computers, a library area, a lounge, and two reservable reflection rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Memorial Union’s second floor and available to Iowa State students, staff, faculty, and other university-community members.

cards.title: Reset or Meet at The Center
cards.subtitle: A fourth-floor Memorial Union space with work screens, small-group seating, and sensory rooms
cards.notes: Plug into an extra screen for coursework, gather at the tables for a small project, or use the quiet sensory room when you need fewer stimuli.
cards.short_summary: The Center pairs practical study equipment with social seating and quieter wellbeing-oriented spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Multicultural Student Affairs says The Center offers computers, plug-in screens, public seating, a small meeting room, a private sensory area, and a quiet sensory room for students.
cards.access_notes: Located in Memorial Union room 4600 on floor four; posted hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., with after-hours access by request.

cards.entity_name: George A. Jackson Black Cultural Center
cards.title: Plan an Organization Gathering at the BCC
cards.subtitle: A reservable student-organization space beside campus on Welch Avenue
cards.notes: Submit the reservation form before planning a meeting or program, then wait for confirmation and review the center’s cancellation requirements.
cards.short_summary: The BCC gives registered organizations a named setting for meetings, programs, and community-building activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State describes the George A. Jackson Black Cultural Center as a programmatic space for all student organizations and provides an online reservation process.
cards.source_title: George A. Jackson Black Cultural Center
cards.access_notes: Located at 517 Welch Avenue; reservations require confirmation, and recognized organizations face weekly room and time limits.

cards.title: Take Cross-Major Work to the Innovation Center
cards.subtitle: Open collaboration areas, study zones, club workshops, and makerspaces
cards.notes: Start in an open study or collaboration zone, then check the relevant training rules before planning hands-on work in any makerspace.
cards.short_summary: The five-level center gives students from different disciplines room to meet, study, design, and build.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State says the Student Innovation Center contains collaborative workspaces, hands-on materials labs, student-club workshop space, and research and development equipment.
cards.access_notes: The building is at 1805 Collaboration Place; open collaboration areas and specialized labs may have different access or training requirements.

cards.title: Pause Beside Janus Agri Altar
cards.subtitle: A tree-filled courtyard intended for study and reflection
cards.notes: Bring reading for a short outdoor session, or pause by Beverly Pepper’s Janus Agri Altar and use the courtyard as a screen-free reset.
cards.short_summary: Trees and a major campus artwork create a quieter outdoor alternative to indoor study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: An Iowa State wellbeing guide identifies Agronomy Hall Courtyard as a quiet, tree-filled place where students, staff, and visitors can study or pause.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor courtyard access is weather-dependent; the cited university guide does not state operating hours or nighttime access.

cards.title: Take Homework Into Reiman Gardens
cards.subtitle: A 17-acre campus garden with indoor and outdoor places to decompress
cards.notes: Show student eligibility at entry, choose a garden setting for reading or a break, and check current visitor information before heading over.
cards.short_summary: The gardens offer students a substantial change of scenery without leaving the Iowa State campus area.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa State describes Reiman Gardens as a 17-acre, year-round campus oasis where students can bring homework or take a break, with free admission for Iowa State students.
cards.access_notes: The university states admission is free for Iowa State students; visitors should verify current garden hours and student-identification requirements before arrival.
